project.name: Experience Proof and Polish
project.summary: Prove that the shipped UR Lessons (hero) versus GW Allies (villain) experience remains playable, responsive, recoverable, accessible, and visually intact through repeatable gates against the real release stack, so regressions fail evidence checks instead
project.definition: Prove that the shipped UR Lessons (hero) versus GW Allies (villain) experience remains playable, responsive, recoverable, accessible, and visually intact through repeatable gates against the real release stack, so regressions fail evidence checks instead of becoming subjective cleanup.

krs.text: A deterministic release-stack end-to-end suite reaches terminal across scenarios that collectively surface every prompt family reachable in UR Lessons versus GW Allies and proves reconnect/resume, stale-command rejection, duplicate-command idempotency, checkpoint recovery, and replay equivalence.

A named reference device, OS, browser, and release-build profile has numeric budgets for cold launch-to-playable, input acknowledgement, authority response, animation frame pacing, and peak memory; repeatable measurements fail documented regression thresholds.

The complete selected matchup is operable keyboard-only and under reduced motion, with automated contrast and accessibility checks plus screen-reader assertions for every prompt, status transition, and game result.

Versioned visual references cover every prompt family and key board, recovery, and terminal states; a clean release-build playthrough has zero unexpected visual diffs, broken curated assets, runtime console errors, or network-dependent play assets.

task.name: Add versioned visual references to the release prompt matrix
task.description: Build on merged W2-209 and its deterministic release-stack prompt matrix. Capture committed, versioned Playwright screenshot references for every reachable UR Lessons versus GW Allies prompt family and key board, reconnect-status, and terminal states across the two fixed scenarios. Use a deterministic viewport, color scheme, fonts, reduced motion or animation settling, and local curated assets; run through the real release preview stack. Fail on unexpected diffs, missing baselines, broken, fallback, or remote assets, public-network play requests, page or console errors, or nonterminal scenario drift. Document the intentional baseline-update workflow and run the gate in CI. Preserve existing product visuals and authority; do not redesign, add decks, add recovery protocol semantics, change performance budgets, or claim real assistive-technology automation. Every Python command must use uv.
